channel.title: Television POV(Greenlight)
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Television POV(Greenlight)" - 7 billion POV's in one TV.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique. After several days of brainstorming I came up with the idea of a researcher obsessed with finding his own point of view. He'd try to use d-classes to flip the channels for him. Once that proves to be ineffective as they'd only be able to get a couple million in a year, he opts to find ways to dampen the signal, he'd find out that a lead-lined room works and it decreases the range considerably to around 40 kilometers. After that he discovers a d-class pov, he'd get the d-class to stare into the tv. The d-class does and enters into the trance. The researcher shuts off the tv and after five minutes the d-class comes to, but the d-class can't remember anything, much to the researcher's frustration. Several days later, the d-class kills himself.

This piques the researcher's interest even more. "what did he see that compelled him to commit suicide?" So, much to the dismay of the other researchers, he finds his own pov.

The ending is from another researcher who writes that the first researcher looked very unaware of his surroundings, suffered terrible disassociation and ultimately killed himself. Concludes that any researcher who wishes to test the SCP must do under supervision from another researcher.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM

The premise here is an interesting one depending on what you do with it. It would be very easy to turn this into a "thing that does a thing" with nothing else - essentially that's what the anomaly is - but if you do something interesting narratively and really explore the effects of this anomaly properly, I think this could be an interesting premise for an article.

Exploring a series of unique vignettes could work, but you'd need to find a way to build them towards a conclusive end that leaves the reader feeling satisfied, and that won't be super easy to do. I'd recommend trying to build a more traditional narrative for your first article. Give us a clear series of events that you're going to tell - that's the core of any good SCP article, a clear narrative. If you've got that, you're on a strong start. The anomaly doesn't necessarily lend itself to a traditional narrative without a bit of work, but you've started that process by having it create an effect in people who watch their own perspective. Try to expand on that in terms of what stories you might tell with it, perhaps. Maybe it causes some serious problems that the Foundation then has to solve, or perhaps it's an addictive feeling, or maybe the Foundation thinks they can use the SCP to try and control people and anomalies in some way.

Whatever you go with, the core thing this needs is a clearer central narrative, with a beginning, middle, and end. What's the story you're going to tell here, in detail? That's the key.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded: Thank you for the critique. Unfortunately for me, there are thousands of SCP articles already written and I don't know all of them. Those are really cool ideas and you can totally make your own SCP with that kind of premise.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Instead of another person, it could spy on every SCP that exists. That alone would be REALLY interesting for the Foundation. And you could explore the reactions of people and SCPs. It could, for instance, show the face of SCP-096 (Shy Guy) to someone, and he rampages after the person. The Foundation could discover the anomalous object like that.

You could also explore the feelings of people that way, nirvana for instance if they saw SCP-5974 (It's the end of the world as we know it) , or dread if they stop at the SCP-3001 (Red Reality).

Hope you get the greenlight! Have a great day!

item.title: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a 4k HDTV with a standard TV remote. When you switch the input to HDMI-1 you can see a POV of a random person in the world. Changing the channel would change the POV to another random individual.

Central Narrative: The article would explore several unique circumstances, like a POV of someone dying, someone who needs glasses, someone tripping on hallucinogens, someone dreaming, someone with color-blindness, etcetera.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The chances of you finding your own POV out of 7 billion people would be virtually impossible. So I'd describe a process where SCP scientists use several d-class's to keep flipping through channels until they come across somebody who worked for the SCP foundation. They'd be found and then asked to stare in front of the TV. What happens is essentially they'd be staring at an infinite mirror, the user of this circumstance would enter into a trance and would require a third party to get them away from the TV. The person in question would eventually wake up and explain what exactly they felt.

Additional Notes: What kind of feelings would they experience? Nirvana? Dread? Would they want to immediately kill themselves? I know that's kind of played out but I want to make sure I hit all the beats.
